title: Brussels makes Benelux history with first-ever small ball double win
content:
While Gaelic football has been organised on a regional basis in the Benelux since 2007, the equivalent hurling and camogie championships are a more recent, post-COVID development. The 2026 small-ball season will be played over three regional rounds, with clubs competing locally in both codes before points accumulated across the series determine the overall champions. 

At the continental level, the European championship remains the primary stage for small-ball competition, but the regional Benelux series has quickly become an important platform for the clubs in the region to sharpen their tools for the Pan-European games and the growing 15-a-side championships.
______

**Round 1 of 2026** was extra special as it took place in the shadow of Europe's greatest Gaelic Games achievement to date, as [Leinster Special Junior Champions](https://www.longfordleader.ie/news/gaa/1949850/last-gasp-winner-as-amsterdam-pip-understrength-longford-slashers-for-leinster-hurling-title.html), [Amsterdam GAC](https://www.instagram.com/amsterdamgac/) lined out in their first outing since their triumphant 15-a-side campaign in Ireland.

But by the end of a memorable day in The Hague, it was [Brussels](https://www.instagram.com/p/DWeGWE0jJnw/?img_index=1) who had made history of their own. In a landmark performance, Brussels became the first club to complete the hurling & camogie double since the regional championship was introduced in 2022. They did so in emphatic fashion, going unbeaten in both competitions and setting an early marker for the season ahead.

Their camogie campaign was outstanding from the first whistle. Brussels won all four of their group games, scoring 59 and conceding just 8, before finishing with a flourish in the final, where they defeated [Eindhoven](https://www.instagram.com/eindhovengaa/) by 9-03 to 0-02. It was dominance from start to finish, and richly deserved silverware to match.

![image](https://udzsj3px04tot0xe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/news/1775041684372-2025%201004%20%20%28233%29.JPG)

If the camogie success was commanding, the hurling win carried extra significance. Brussels again topped the group with a perfect record, scoring 59 and conceding 14 across their four matches. That set up a final against Amsterdam, whose recent achievements have placed them in the history books of Global GAA. Amsterdam are undefeated in European 15-a-side hurling, have won the last two Benelux hurling titles, and arrived in The Hague as Leinster champions, but Brussels rose to the challenge superbly, claiming the decider by 2-12 to 0-07.

![image](https://udzsj3px04tot0xe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/news/1775043569692-2025%201004%20%20%2883%29.JPG)

Across the day, the standard of play was reflected in the numbers. The camogie competition produced 40 goals and 58 points across 12 matches, while the hurling yielded 38 goals and 126 points in 13 games. Yet for all the scores and spectacle, the enduring image from Round 1 will be Brussels standing alone as the first club to lift both titles in the same season.

There was also another encouraging development in the presence of [Paris Gaels](https://www.instagram.com/paris_gaels_gaa/reels/), whose participation in both codes was a welcome sign of the games’ continued spread in France. The growth of clubs with strong non-Irish playing bases is one of the most exciting aspects of Gaelic games in Europe, and Paris’ involvement was another reminder that the future of hurling and camogie on the continent will be shaped by an ever-broader community.

____________

**Round 1 in The Hague delivered quality, history, and a significant changing of the guard. Amsterdam arrived as champions of Leinster, but it was Brussels who left with a Benelux first.**

**Camogie – final standings**
1. Brussels
2. Eindhoven
3. Amsterdam
4. Den Haag
5. Paris Gaels

**Camogie – key stats**
- Brussels topped the group with 4 wins from 4
- Brussels scored 59 and conceded 8 in the group stage
- Camogie final: Brussels 9-03, Eindhoven 0-02
- Total across the competition: 12 matches, 40 goals, 58 points

**Hurling – final standings**
1. Brussels
2. Amsterdam
3. Eindhoven
4. Den Haag
5. Paris

**Hurling – key stats**
- Brussels topped the group with 4 wins from 4
- Brussels scored 59 and conceded 14 in the group stage
- Hurling final: Brussels 2-12, Amsterdam 0-07
- Total across the competition: 13 matches, 38 goals, 126 points


The Benelux would also like to extend sincere thanks to our new sponsor for their valued support - [Breagh recruitment](https://breaghrecruitment.com/) and to our photographer @[brt.photo](https://www.instagram.com/brt.photo/) for capturing the day so well. Support like this is hugely important to the continued growth of hurling and camogie across the region, and it is greatly appreciated.

title: The Breagh Benelux Round 1 opens 2026 season in style in Maastricht
content:
Benelux Round 1 in Maastricht provided a strong opening to the 2026 season, bringing **together 13 clubs across 18 teams** and amalgamations for a packed day of Ladies and Men’s football. Across 41 matches, teams produced 11 hours and 24 minutes of playing time, with a combined scoring return of 151 goals and 374 points — an impressive reflection of both the scale of the event and the competitive standard on show in the first of four rounds.

The figures were striking across both grades. The Ladies competition accounted for 15 matches, 3 hours and 29 minutes of play, 62 goals and 135 points, while the Men’s competition delivered 26 matches, 7 hours and 55 minutes of action, with 89 goals and 239 points scored. There were also standout scoring returns from some of the day’s strongest performers, with Brussels Craobh Rua finishing as the top-scoring side in the Ladies grade on 104, while Luxembourg A led the way in the Men’s competition with 84.
_________

![image](https://udzsj3px04tot0xe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/news/1774995020650-_DSC1974.jpg)

**[Brussels Craobh Rua](https://www.instagram.com/brussels_gaa/) set the pace in the Ladies competition**

The Ladies competition produced a clear early storyline, with Brussels setting the standard from the outset and carrying that form all the way to Cup success.

They topped Group 1 with two wins from two, opening with two dominant victories over an amalgamation of Leuven/Den Haag/Frankfurt, and against Eindhoven Shamrocks. That left them comfortably clear at the top of the group, having shown their attacking strength from the very beginning of the day.

Eindhoven Shamrocks also progressed from Group 1 after their 7-11 to 3-01 win over Leuven/Haag/Frankfurt secured second place.

![image](https://udzsj3px04tot0xe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/news/1775035523882-_Z621406.jpg)

In Group 2, [GSC Luxembourg](https://www.instagram.com/p/DTnOr2MjOzQ/) produced the most consistent group-stage campaign, taking three wins from three to finish top of the table. Their victories came against Amsterdam/Aachen, Maastricht/Nijmegen, and Groningen/Cologne, while Groningen/Cologne also advanced to the Cup semi-finals after wins over both Maastricht/Nijmegen and Amsterdam/Aachen.

If the main trend in the groups was Brussels scoring power, the knockout stages only reinforced it. In the Cup semi-finals, the Belgian side defeated Groningen/Cologne by 4-05 to 2-02, while Eindhoven Shamrocks overcame GSC Luxembourg by 2-10 to 0-03 to book their place in the final.

That set up a decider between the top two teams from Group 1, but there was no slowing Brussels down. They produced another emphatic display in the Cup Final, defeating Eindhoven with ease to claim the Round 1 title in commanding fashion.

The Ladies Shield went to Maastricht/Nijmegen, who defeated Leuven/Haag/Frankfurt by 4-03 to 2-04 in the final.

![image](https://udzsj3px04tot0xe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/news/1775035680538-_DSC1999%20%281%29.jpg)

**Luxembourg A pull through a hard-fought Men’s round**

The Men’s competition was deeper and more varied across the day, but by the end of it Luxembourg A had found a way through a highly competitive field to take the main honours.

In Group 1, [Eindhoven](https://www.instagram.com/eindhovengaa/) A set the pace with three wins from three to finish top on nine points. They were joined in the Cup semi-finals by the student side - Groningen Gaels, who secured second place ahead of Frankfurt/Cologne/Düsseldorf and Den Haag/Aachen.

![image](https://udzsj3px04tot0xe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/news/1775035952024-Great%20Photo%201.jpg)

Group 2 saw Maastricht/Nijmegen produce one of the strongest group-stage runs of the day, also finishing with three wins from three to top the table. 

Group 3 was more finely balanced. Amsterdam/Eindhoven B finished top, level on points with Luxembourg A, with score difference separating the sides after the two teams had shared the points in their group meeting. Both advanced to the Cup semi-finals, while Luxembourg B/Leuven B and Brussels B moved into the Plate competition.

The knockout stages produced some of the best football of the day. In the Cup semi-finals, Luxembourg A edged Eindhoven A by 1-08 to 1-06, while Amsterdam/Eindhoven B defeated Maastricht/Nijmegen by 2-06 to 0-08.

![image](https://udzsj3px04tot0xe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/news/1775036062002-_Z620749.jpg)


That set up a final between two sides who had already proven difficult to separate earlier in the day, and the decider lived up to that billing. In what was one of the standout contests of the round, Luxembourg A overcame Amsterdam/Eindhoven B by 2-08 to 1-09 in a final that was tight, intense and hard fought throughout.

The Men’s Shield was won by Leuven A, who defeated Groningen Gaels by 1-09 to 1-07, while Frankfurt/Cologne/Düsseldorf claimed the Plate.

**Strong start across both grades!**

Taken as a whole, Benelux Round 1 offered exactly the kind of opening the championship would have wanted: strong participation, a high volume of games, impressive scoring returns and competitive football across both grades.

In the Ladies competition, Brussels Craobh Rua set the early benchmark with a dominant run to Cup success, while Maastricht/Nijmegen left the day with Shield honours. In the Men’s competition, Luxembourg A came through the toughest moments to take the Cup, with Leuven A and Frankfurt/Cologne/Düsseldorf also claiming silverware.

As the first of four rounds in the 2026 series, Maastricht delivered both an immediate competitive snapshot and a strong platform for what promises to be another busy Benelux season.

Thanks also to local photographer @[brt.photo](https://www.instagram.com/brt.photo?igsh=MThmdXo1enYxNG1paQ==)

title: Breagh Recruitment Partners with Benelux Championships for 2026 Season
content:
Gaelic Games Europe and the Benelux Division are delighted to announce the launch of the [Breagh Recruitment](https://breaghrecruitment.com/) Benelux Championship Season for 2026, marking an exciting new partnership that will support Gaelic Games across the region.

The collaboration between Gaelic Games Europe and Breagh Recruitment reflects a shared commitment to community, ambition and supporting people striving to achieve more. Following a recent meeting with the Breagh Recruitment team, it was clear that the partnership is built on common values — hard work, resilience and backing communities to perform whatever the conditions.

![image](https://youtu.be/MMa276pOFI0)

The Breagh Recruitment Benelux Championships will see clubs from across the region compete in football, LGFA, hurling and camogie competitions throughout the season, across both 11-a-side and 15-a-side formats. The championship calendar will culminate in the Benelux Finals in Eindhoven this September, where the region’s top teams will battle for silverware.

The partnership comes at a particularly exciting moment for Gaelic Games in the Benelux region.

The Benelux board is preparing for its first-ever Go Games series this weekend, while also gearing up to host the largest European Féile ever organised. Later this year, the region will once again send representative teams to compete at the GAA World Games, marking the second time Benelux players will take part on the global stage.

All of this momentum comes in the shadow of a historic achievement for the region, as [Amsterdam GAC captured the Leinster Special Junior Cup](https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2025/1124/1545513-mcdermott-relieved-after-amsterdams-leinster-win/), becoming the first Benelux club to win the prestigious competition and further underlining the growing strength of Gaelic Games in mainland Europe.

Chris Collins, Head of Operations at Gaelic Games Europe, welcomed the partnership announcement.

“We are extremely grateful to Breagh Recruitment for their support of Gaelic Games in Europe. Their investment in the Benelux Championships will have a real impact on participation and development across the region. Partnerships like this allow our clubs and volunteers to continue building strong Gaelic Games communities throughout Europe and we are excited about using this additional support to deliver some excellent games development initiatives with the regional board and clubs.”

Breagh Recruitment also expressed their enthusiasm about becoming involved with the Gaelic Games community across the Benelux region.

Cathal McKeever of Breagh Recruitment said:

“At Breagh Recruitment we believe in backing people and communities that are striving to achieve more. The GAA has a unique ability to bring people together and we are delighted to support Gaelic Games Europe and the Benelux region. We are looking forward to attending as many rounds of games as possible and connecting with the community and its members.”

Adding a fun twist to the new partnership, the Breagh Recruitment team have also launched an office sweepstake, selecting the clubs they believe will come out on top during the championship season. With strong competition across the region, it remains to be seen whether one of the traditional powerhouses will dominate or if an underdog story will unfold over the course of the year.

![image](https://youtube.com/shorts/ld_vJIisp-g?feature=share)


Across the season, clubs will travel throughout the region competing in championship rounds that will determine who reaches the Benelux Finals later this year.

title: New Club Spotlight – Aachen Gaels
author: Alan Fitzgerald
content:
Germany's first new GAA club in a decade has emerged at the crossroads of Germany, Belgium, and the Netherlands.

Aachen Gaels brings Germany's total to 12 clubs, making it the third-largest GAA nation in continental Europe.

The club was founded in late 2025 by a group of Irish expatriates working at RWTH Aachen University and local tech companies. Their inaugural training session drew over 30 participants, a promising start for the fledgling club.

"We've been overwhelmed by the response," said club chairperson Siobhan Murphy. "There's clearly a hunger for GAA in this part of Germany."

The Gaels have already registered for the 2026 Benelux Championships and are actively recruiting players of all skill levels.
